scope: Standard table More actions captions and dropdown glyphs in Linux ru/en. Complete toolbar comparisons remain rejected and are retained below. Existing full grid/pagination, ordinary/primary button, layout and style regressions remain strict.

nativeInputs.scope: Complete standard table toolbar strip, including the shadow row. Reuses eight previously captured native images of four XML-only forms. Grid/chips/form shell outside this strip.

implementation: Table More actions uses the existing regular button fill, FreeType caption composition and border component; other dropdown consumers retain their previous path.
The caption uses a measured 4 px trailing allocation, moving its bitmap 2 px left. Default NativeCaption trailing allocation remains zero.
NativeButtonArrow composes a 6x3 asymmetric alpha stencil over the shared discrete button gradient, resolving both standard/style CSS colors through getComputedStyle.
The arrow is calibrated only for 26 px buttons; unsupported height/color keeps the browser arrow and records the existing localized text-approximation notice.
Both actual detached windows and complete dirty replacements retain the same table DOM and selected identity; viewing saves no XML.

intermediateCandidates.note: Native button fill/caption was enabled first; caption placement and browser dropdown glyph still differed.
Caption placement was corrected; arrow initially fell back because a CSS variable string was parsed before CSS resolution. Fixed by reading the computed canvas color.

observations.note: Selecting the table adds a blue outline across the first two strip rows; the screenshot also preserves changed lower button-border pixels. Its 892 differing pixels are recorded, not waived.

nativeReadonlySearchRepeat.statement: The yellow search outline survives root selection, search/body clicks and Escape on this recorded ReadOnly form. Default remains gray under the same actions. No general color rule or metadata applicability is inferred from these observations.

remaining: Complete toolbar strips still differ: search placeholder/clear button and outline states, standard icons, grouped button fill/borders, and the known lower-border paint differences. No toolbar pixels are masked or waived.
Other menu consumers/states, fonts/sizes, customized palettes and complete table forms remain open.
Windows, other DPI and native property inventory remain unaccepted.
